report_metadata.title: Reconstructing ES from 58,988,994 market events
report_metadata.subtitle: A Rust and Node market-data engineering case study: bounded acquisition, streaming decode, order-book reconstruction, independent validation, and measured performance.
report_metadata.evidence_scope: One bounded 23-hour ES Globex session and one measured host

claims.label: Records streamed
claims.method_note: Sum of the four schema record counts after checksum, schema, and count verification.
claims.limitations: Bounded to the named historical session and four acquired schemas.

claims.label: Conservatively counted acquisition cost
claims.method_note: Quote-first acquisition with a hard 10 USD cap and conservative spend accounting before external calls.
claims.limitations: Per-schema public display costs are rounded; this total preserves the promoted conservative ledger value.

claims.label: Exact eligible MBP-10 updates
claims.method_note: Records were merge-grouped by exact event timestamp, publisher, instrument, and sequence. Identical action, price, and size records were paired within each group. Trades compared the reconstructed pre-event book; state-changing events compared the final event book. State remained withheld until a complete clear/snapshot baseline, and every eligible MBP-10 miss remained in the denominator.
claims.limitations: Top-of-book agreement only; this is not full-depth, routing, or execution-quality proof.

claims.label: End-to-end exact match
claims.method_note: Exact price-and-size matches divided by all eligible MBP-10 updates.
claims.limitations: Measured after the explicit complete-baseline boundary for one session.

claims.label: Compressed MBO streaming throughput
claims.method_note: Median of five measured fresh child processes after one discarded warmup; compressed, streaming, single-thread MBO.
claims.limitations: Warm page cache and one measured host; not a cross-platform guarantee.

claims.label: Decoded MBO throughput
claims.method_note: Decoded throughput for the same compressed, streaming, single-thread MBO benchmark row.
claims.limitations: Warm page cache and one measured host; not a cross-platform guarantee.

claims.label: Heuristic sweep events
claims.method_note: A publisher-qualified trade at least four ticks beyond the prior 50-trade high or low opened one candidate in that direction. A later trade had to cross back through the swept level within five seconds.
claims.limitations: This is a transparent historical-data heuristic, not a trading signal or execution recommendation. Visible resting-size attribution does not estimate hidden liquidity. The result is bounded to the named instrument session and committed parameters.

claims.label: Measured benchmark configurations
claims.method_note: Count of measured configuration rows in the promoted benchmark matrix.
claims.limitations: One additional high-memory configuration is explicitly unsupported.

claims.label: Rust and Node parity records
claims.method_note: The host Node native binding and Rust CLI decoded the same live MBO input. Record counts matched, and every emitted sweep field matched across both language surfaces.
claims.limitations: This proves parity for the measured host, session, schema, and detector configuration. It is not hosted cross-platform package-release proof.

validation.methodology: Records were merge-grouped by exact event timestamp, publisher, instrument, and sequence. Identical action, price, and size records were paired within each group. Trades compared the reconstructed pre-event book; state-changing events compared the final event book. State remained withheld until a complete clear/snapshot baseline, and every eligible MBP-10 miss remained in the denominator.

sweep.methodology: A publisher-qualified trade at least four ticks beyond the prior 50-trade high or low opened one candidate in that direction. A later trade had to cross back through the swept level within five seconds.
limitations: This is a transparent historical-data heuristic, not a trading signal or execution recommendation.
Visible resting-size attribution does not estimate hidden liquidity.
The result is bounded to the named instrument session and committed parameters.

parity.methodology: The host Node native binding and Rust CLI decoded the same live MBO input. Record counts matched, and every emitted sweep field matched across both language surfaces.
limitations: This proves parity for the measured host, session, schema, and detector configuration.
It is not hosted cross-platform package-release proof.

benchmark.methodology: Each configuration runs in a fresh child process. One warmup is discarded and at least five measured runs are aggregated with median, nearest-rank p95, and population standard deviation. Timings include file reads, decompression, DBN parsing, record traversal, thread startup, and joins. Parallel rows decode independent identical streams and report aggregate throughput.

capabilities.detail: Every configuration is warmed explicitly before recorded child runs.
The managed WSL run has no safe, isolated OS page-cache eviction primitive; no cold numbers are fabricated.
Each child reads its own Linux /proc/self/status VmHWM value.
The forbid-unsafe workspace does not install a global allocator shim; results use null rather than zero.
Parallel rows run independent streams, because one DBN/Zstd stream is sequential and is not falsely presented as splittable.

unsupported_configurations.reason: planned input buffers total 35579770848 bytes, above the configured 17179869184-byte safety gate

limitations: The measured evidence covers one historical ES instrument session and one host.
Benchmark measurements used a warm page cache; cold-cache performance is unsupported.
Validation proves reconstructed top-of-book equality, not full-depth equality.
The sweep detector is a transparent heuristic, not a signal, P&L claim, or execution recommendation.
The report does not claim hidden-liquidity estimation, exchange connectivity, routing, or production trading.
Provider timeout and interrupted-download behavior has not been fault-injected against the paid API.
Hosted cross-platform native-package and public deployment proof is not yet part of this evidence.

book_replay.label: Synthetic teaching example
book_replay.description: An invented ten-step sequence demonstrates baseline withholding, event-boundary comparison, invalidation, and recovery. It is not sampled from purchased data.

events.explanation: A clear begins a new baseline. The book is not yet trustworthy.
A bid arrives, but the snapshot event is incomplete.
The final snapshot record establishes a complete two-sided baseline.
A lower bid is added without changing the top bid.
A state-changing event is compared after its complete event boundary.
A trade is compared with the pre-event book before associated mutations.
The paired mutation reduces displayed ask size after the trade comparison.
A malformed or incomplete boundary invalidates the reconstructed state.
Recovery begins from a new complete snapshot, not from stale state.
The completed replacement snapshot restores trustworthy state.
